title: Minimax Estimation of a Common Causal Risk Ratio under Rare Baseline Risks
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Math referee passed; historical priority against Greenland-Robins1985 remains unresolved.
gap_reasons: Greenland--Robins (1985) is the closest sparse common-RR comparator, but its unavailable full theorem scope leaves the claimed finite-sample all-procedure rare-risk frontier unpositioned theorem-by-theorem; obtain and compare its exact quantifiers before claiming novelty.

Efficient calibration is established only on fixed-alphabet interior sequences through exhaustive enumeration of (4K)^n samples, leaving no scalable calibration procedure demonstrated for the sparse growing-strata regime.

proof_attempt_summary: Recovered the interrupted D-1.2 run, derived the same-class rare-risk ratio minimax and honest-length frontiers, repaired the D0 algebraic defect, and verified three cited textbook statements. The latest D0.5 math referee passed with no findings; the decision referee revised only for unavailable Greenland-Robins1985 full-text priority comparison. An independent main-owned validity gate confirmed discovery-stage soundness and below-field novelty (subfield, score6.6 versus7.4), so the run stopped under the standing downgraded-bank policy; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: On known uniform strata with unknown bounded propensities and baseline risks in a public rare envelope, the common causal risk ratio has minimax squared error \(R\asymp s\) and minimax uniformly \(90\%\)-honest connected expected length \(L_{.90}\asymp\sqrt{s}\), where \(s=\min\{1,(n\rho)^{-1}+K/(n^2\rho)\}\). Total original-record procedures attain these orders, and legal singleton-matched multiplicative priors prove both converses on the same class. Uniform consistency holds exactly when \(n\rho\to\infty\) and \(n^2\rho/K\to\infty\). The class is a proper subclass of the positive common-RR model anchored by Richardson--Robins--Wang (2017). At \(\rho_n=1/(8n)\), the converse transfers upward: every estimator has worst-case squared risk at least \(1/32768\), and every uniformly honest connected interval has worst-case expected length at least \(1/128\) on the range-restricted positive published model. Positivity alone therefore permits neither uniform consistency nor uniformly shrinking honest intervals there; upper guarantees remain on the stated subclass. Exact localized calibration also combines global honesty with efficient endpoints and expected length on the declared regular sequences.
gap: Greenland--Robins establishes sparse common-RR consistency and dual-regime variance in its verified abstract, and Sato develops common-RR estimating functions and approximate Fieller inference. Zeng et al. supplies additive-effect collision machinery. None of the full theorem texts inspected states the specified all-procedure rare-risk and original-occupancy decision frontier; Greenland--Robins full text remains externally unverifiable.
fill: The finite-sample obligations give explicit attainment, same-class estimation and honest-length converses, and an arbitrary-sequence consistency characterization. The first-class open calibration question isolates the stronger empirical-to-efficient inference bridge rather than portraying the supplied complete rate argument as an unsolved lemma.
